teaser.text: Sun Hung Kai Properties Limited builds places, sells some of them and keeps others to earn rent. Its business is therefore a cycle of investing in land and buildings, collecting money from many kinds of users, and deciding how much cash to reinvest, repay or distribute.

stock.title: SHKP stock forecast
stock.meta_description: SHKP's weighted forecast reaches HK$110.48 by October 2029, with bear and bull scenarios tied to earnings, rents and debt.
stock.opening: The weighted forecast puts SHKP at HK$110.48 in October 2029, a positive 15% return, after HK$92.06 in October 2027 and HK$98.94 in October 2028. It hinges on improving project earnings, leasing and debt reduction despite execution and market risks.
stock.closing: The full SHKP memo also answers questions about SHKP's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could SHKP's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast points to a weak first year, a flat second year and a moderate three-year gain after dividends. The weighted price is HK$92.06 in October 2027, HK$98.94 in October 2028 and HK$110.48 in October 2029, equivalent to returns of negative 10%, roughly zero and positive 15%. By the last date, the bear-to-bull range is HK$55.88 to HK$175.90, against today’s HK$106.30.

blocks.heading: What has to go right—and wrong—for SHKP?

paragraphs.text: The bear case assumes a slow Hong Kong recovery, continued Mainland office weakness, lower-margin handovers and spending ahead of rent. Operating profit reaches only HK$23,000 million by the last date, net debt rises to HK$79,559 million and the multiple settles at 10.5x. The price falls from HK$64.27 in the first window to HK$55.88 in October 2029, including dividends. Its 30% probability reflects four years of declining operating income, weaker development results and uncertain repeatability of recent cash conversion.

The bull case requires stronger housing demand, better project margins, successful West Kowloon leasing and continued growth in Mainland retail and data centres. Operating profit reaches HK$33,500 million, net debt falls to HK$26,291 million and the multiple reaches 16.0x. The shares rise from HK$122.76 to HK$175.90. Its 18% probability is lower because new capacity needs capital before mature rent arrives, while FY2026 development results were weaker.

blocks.heading: How much cash does SHKP really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow deducts capital spending and lease payments from operating cash flow. Interest is not deducted again because finance costs already appear within operating activities; subtracting them twice would understate cash generation. Capital spending also has two meanings: some maintains existing earning power, while some creates new malls, offices or data centres.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for SHKP today?

paragraphs.text: The forward P/E of 12.7 times implies roughly HK$8.37 of earnings per share over the next twelve months. Against FY2026 reported earnings of HK$7.39, that suggests about 13% growth. Against underlying earnings of HK$7.89, the gap is about 6%, although the definitions differ.

dividend.title: SHKP dividend: history, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: SHKP paid HK$3.91 per share for FY2026; cash coverage has varied, and the dividend yield is 3.7% at HK$106.30.
dividend.opening: SHKP’s FY2026 annual dividend was HK$3.91 per share. In FY2022, dividends of HK$14,344 million exceeded free cash flow of HK$1,582 million, so cash coverage has not been consistent.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers SHKP’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does SHKP pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: SHKP cut its annual dividend by 24% in FY2024. For FY2026 it paid HK$0.98 per share at the interim stage and proposed HK$2.93 as the final payment, bringing the annual amount to HK$3.91 under a 40%–50% underlying-profit payout policy. Underlying profit excludes unrealised investment-property valuation changes but can include gains realised when properties are sold. It is therefore steadier than reported profit, but not necessarily pure recurring rent.

blocks.heading: Is SHKP’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Profit and cash are different. A developer may recognise a sale while land and construction bills fall due at another time. In FY2022, free cash flow was HK$1,582 million against dividends paid of HK$14,344 million, so the shortfall had to come from reserves, borrowing or other transactions. Dividends exceeded free cash flow again in FY2023 and FY2024.

The pattern changed in FY2025 and FY2026. More cash remained inside the business, and SHKP repaid substantially more debt than it issued. Acquisitions were a smaller cash use than businesses and assets sold, while there were no share buybacks or proceeds from new shares in the five years. Shareholders therefore received their direct cash return mainly through dividends.

paragraphs.text: Dividends are HK$3.91 per share in October 2027 in all cases. That combines the declared final payment with an assumed interim payment. The base path then rises to HK$4.00 and HK$4.10 as earnings recover and the payout reaches the upper end of the stated range. The bear path falls to HK$3.20 and HK$3.00 at the lower payout rate; the bull path reaches HK$4.30 and HK$4.60 with stronger earnings. The prior fall from HK$4.95 to HK$3.75 shows the risk.

blocks.heading: What is SHKP’s dividend yield at today’s price?

paragraphs.text: The trend is mixed: FY2026 revenue grew 18.2%, while operating margin fell to 26.7%. Net debt fell to HK$66,767 million. Computed as cash from operations minus capital spending, SHKP’s real free cash flow per share reached HK$13.25 after a HK$23,554 million working-capital release. Diluted EPS was HK$7.39, below HK$8.82 in 2022. At HK$106.30, shares carry a 12.5% free cash flow yield. The dividend yield is 3.7%.
